title: PowerShell opened LSASS with full access on scranton (credential dumping)
rationale: All describe the same action: PowerShell.exe (PID 2976, user pbeesly) opening lsass.exe (PID 736) on scranton.dmevals.local at 2020-05-02T03:05:16 with GrantedAccess 0x1FFFFF/0x1F3FFF, the access mask used to read LSASS memory for credential dumping. F08, F33, F36, F47 and F52 add surrounding context (private-key export, exfil script, stager) but center on the same LSASS handle event.

title: Remote PowerShell session opened LSASS with full access on nashua
rationale: Same action on nashua.dmevals.local at 2020-05-02T03:09:29: wsmprovhost.exe (PID 7720, PowerShell Remoting host, user pbeesly) opened lsass.exe (PID 728) with GrantedAccess 0x1F3FFF via a PowerShell cmdlet call trace, consistent with reading LSASS credential memory. F10/F20/F34 describe the same handle event.

title: LSASS wrote SAM account data on scranton
rationale: lsass.exe itself set HKLM\SAM\SAM\Domains\Account\F on scranton; consistent with normal OS behavior, no hive-copy activity observed, so recorded as suspicious SAM-database context only.

title: PowerShell Get-Keystrokes keylogger on scranton
rationale: User pbeesly executed Get-Keystrokes with a Keystroke-Check AV-enumeration function and View-Job on scranton, i.e. keylogging input capture.

title: Invoke-ScreenCapture GUI capture on scranton
rationale: pbeesly defined and invoked Invoke-ScreenCapture using System.Windows.Forms/System.Drawing to write screen captures to the Downloads folder, i.e. GUI input capture.

title: WebDAV forced-authentication coercion from scranton to 192.168.0.4
rationale: 10.0.1.4 (scranton) SMB probes to 192.168.0.4 were rejected, then fell back to WebDAV with DavClnt/Microsoft-WebDAV-MiniRedir requests answered 401 before succeeding, i.e. forced authentication to capture credentials.

title: Credential-bearing SMB share access from 10.0.1.4 to SYSVOL/IPC$/ADMIN$
rationale: Same source 10.0.1.4 accessed SYSVOL/IPC$/ADMIN$ on newyork and nashua as SCRANTON$ and pbeesly, consistent with credential-bearing SMB activity accompanying the WebDAV coercion, though such access is also common in legitimate administration.

title: accesschk.exe created a file named passwordsDB on scranton
rationale: accesschk.exe (PID 9204, launched by pbeesly) created C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\passwordsDB; the credential-themed name is suspicious but accesschk is a legitimate ACL tool and no credential content was observed. F28 and F62 describe the same file-creation event.

title: Sysinternals pspasswd credential tooling staged on scranton
rationale: pbeesly's PowerShell wrote pspasswd64.exe/pspasswd.exe into Downloads\SysinternalsSuite; staging credential-manipulation tooling is consistent with credential access via unsecured tooling.

title: Get-PrivateKeys exported machine certificates to .pfx on scranton
rationale: pbeesly ran Get-PrivateKeys, enumerating cert:\LocalMachine and exporting each certificate's private key to .pfx files protected by the hardcoded password 'saribas' — private-key theft. F27 and F64 describe the same script and export action.

title: Kerberos service-ticket requests for krbtgt and machine accounts by pbeesly (RC4)
rationale: pbeesly@DMEVALS.LOCAL requested 4769 TGS tickets for machine accounts and krbtgt with RC4 encryption, consistent with Kerberoasting-style ticket requests.

title: Get-PrivateKeys certificate theft and Invoke-BeachCleanup anti-forensic cleanup
rationale: F58 covers the Get-PrivateKeys export of all LocalMachine certificates to .pfx (certificate theft); F59 covers Invoke-BeachCleanup deleting the exported .pfx and staging artifacts, the anti-forensic complement to the same certificate-theft action.

title: No password spraying; 4648 explicit-credential logons are PsExec lateral movement
rationale: No 4625 events exist, so no spray pattern; the 4648 explicit-credential logons show pbeesly credential reuse with PSEXESVC for lateral movement, not brute force.

title: PsExec with cleartext credentials to NASHUA before LSASS access
rationale: pbeesly repeatedly launched PsExec64.exe against \\NASHUA with the password in cleartext on the command line, i.e. lateral movement using valid credentials, not credential access.

title: Invoke-Exfil WebDAV exfiltration with hardcoded credentials (not MFA interception)
rationale: pbeesly's Invoke-Exfil compresses Downloads and exfiltrates to a WebDAV share using hardcoded credentials; this is credential use and exfiltration, not MFA interception.

title: Adjacent credential/exfil activity is not web session cookie theft
rationale: PsExec with plaintext credentials, Invoke-Exfil to WebDAV, and sdelete cleanup are credential use, exfiltration and anti-forensics, not theft of web session cookies.
